instruction.text: Write in the gap to complete the idiom.

atoms.b: Relax! We'll cross that ((bridge)) when we come to it.

wrong.text: To cross that bridge once you come to it: to deal with a possible issue only once it actually occurs
wrong.sound: To cross that bridge once you come to it means to deal with a possible issue only once it actually occurs.

wrong.text: ignorance is bliss: it's good not to know
wrong.sound: Ignorance is bliss means it's good not to know.

atoms.b: This behaviour describes Germany in a ((nutshell)).
She turned up out of the ((blue)) after six months away.

wrong.sound: Out of the blue means unexpectedly.

wrong.text: when it rains, it pours: multiple alike things happen at once/ one after the other
wrong.sound: When it rains, it pours means that multiple alike things happen at once or one after the other.

atoms.b: Never ((judge)) a book by its cover!

wrong.text: to judge a book by its cover: to judge based on first impressions/ outer appearance
wrong.sound: To judge a book by its cover means to judge based on first impressions or outer appearance.

atoms.b: I've been feeling a bit ((under)) the weather lately.

wrong.text: to feel under the weather: to feel unwell
wrong.sound: To feel under the weather means to feel unwell.

wrong.text: to call it a day: to stop doing something
wrong.sound: To call it a day means to stop doing something.

atoms.b: I didn't want to add ((insult)) to injury.

wrong.text: to add insult to injury: to make a bad situation worse
wrong.sound: To add insult to injury means make a bad situation worse.

atoms.b: Great! Doing that will kill two ((birds)) with one stone.

wrong.text: to kill two birds with one stone: to achieve two things by doing one
wrong.sound: To kill two birds with one stone means achieve two things by doing one.

atoms.b: It's time we finally address the ((elephant)) in the room.

wrong.text: to address the elephant in the room: to talk about the obvious
wrong.sound: To address the elephant in the room means to talk about the obvious.

atoms.b: Wow, this got out of ((hand)) quickly.

wrong.text: to get out of hand: control is lost
wrong.sound: To get out of hand means that control is lost.

atoms.b: I might need some time to wrap my ((head)) around this.

wrong.text: to wrap your head around something: to really understand/believe something
wrong.sound: To wrap your head around something means to really understand or believe something.

atoms.b: Yes, that hits the ((nail)) on the head.

wrong.text: to hit the nail on the head: to be right.
wrong.sound: To hit the nail on the head means to be right.

atoms.b: Are you still on the ((fence)) about going to the cinema tomorrow?

wrong.text: to be on the fence: to be indecisive
wrong.sound: To be on the fence means to be indecisive.
